csv_project_name: Design Services for Campus Wide Assessment
csv_agency: University of New Mexico Dept of Facility Planning
csv_scope_of_work: The University of New Mexico (UNM) is soliciting offers from architectural/engineering firms to furnish, provide, and perform the professional design services as described and identified within this Request for Proposal (RFP) invitation. Please read carefully all instructions, specifications, terms and conditions. Failure to comply with the instructions, specifications, terms and conditions of this RFP may result in your proposal being declared nonresponsive. Develop an implementation plan for attachment A Campus-Level Services o Feasibility & Concept Study: Develop comparative concepts for electrified heating solutions at multiple scales: (a) individual-building conversions, (b) combined building hubs For each, include routing/plant siting, interconnections, looped configurations, temperature/pressure regimes, and controls. o Distribution Concepts & Resiliency: Prepare preliminary alignment drawings indicating corridors, utility/roadway crossings, and constructability impacts to vehicular and pedestrian traffic. Identify isolations, valving, and segmenting to support phased cutovers. o Interconnections: Evaluate opportunities to tie into existing plants or future energy centers; address redundancy and future expansion capacity. o Heat Sources & Recovery: Identify and compare electric-based heat sources (e.g., heat recovery chillers, ambient loop heat pumps), thermal storage, and electric boilers (backup/peaking). Where residual steam is temporarily required, define HX interfaces and a retirement plan. Building-Level Services o For each identified building (see Attachment A), perform: o Records Review & Field Walkthroughs: Confirm major equipment and internal steam distribution use (AHUs/coils, sterilizers, humidification, kitchens, DHW, labs). Document locations and space constraints. o Green/Yellow/Red Classification: o Green: Connection to mechanical room with minimal interior modifications. o Yellow: Connection to mechanical room plus point-of-use steam generation (e.g., local electric steam for sterilizers/humidification). o Red: Significant AHU/coil replacements or major system modifications required. o Steam Loads & Residual Needs: Identify any steam services to remain (process loads, kitchens, specialty research), and propose alternatives where feasible (e.g., humidification via atomizing systems, electric process heat). o Domestic Hot Water (DHW): DHW strategies and HX selections; address Legionella risk management, temperature control, and scald protection. o Schematic Flow Diagrams: For each building category (G/Y/R), provide mechanical flow diagrams and narrative sequences describing conversion strategy, control points, and tie-ins. Analysis, Phasing, and Costing o Load Analysis: High-level analysis using available metering/utility data and verified nameplate/equipment data; indicate data gaps and assumptions. Option Comparison: Provide a transparent comparison of building-by-building, hub-based, and campus LTHW options, including NPV/total-cost-of-ownership, carbon impact, electrical capacity implications, risks, and scalability. o Phasing Plan: Identify building/zone groupings for conversion, required temporary services, and cutover sequences to minimize operational disruption. o Opinion of Probable Cost (OPC): Class 4/5 OPC for each phase, with schedule of values broken into: (a) campus distribution, (b) building conversions by G/Y/R category, (c) heat-source/HR equipment, (d) controls integration, (e) commissioning/turnover. Provide range and confidence level. FEASIBILITY ANALYSIS Reliability & Resiliency: Create looped/segmentable LTHW distribution with clear outage and bypass strategies. Efficiency & Decarbonization: Evaluate pathways to electrify heating (building-level, hub-based,), including heat-recovery chillers, ambient/low-temp loops, and electric boilers for backup; provide a staged roadmap aligned with UNM sustainability goals. Lifecycle Value: Provide total cost of ownership analyses and capital phasing that reduce risk to critical research and patient-care environments. Constructability & Phasing: Develop a realistic plan that protects academic and research continuity and aligns with academic calendars and seasonal constraints.
csv_disciplines_requested: Architecture Services, Interior Design/Space Planning, Programming, Rehabilitation & Refurbishment, Civil Engineering, Construction/Project Management, Mechanical Engineering

title: Design Services for Campus Wide Assessment
short_description: Campus-wide decarbonization and heating electrification assessment for the University of New Mexico.
project_scope: Campus-wide assessment and feasibility study for converting the University of New Mexico heating infrastructure from steam-based systems to electrified low-temperature hot water solutions. Scope includes comparative concepts for individual building conversions and combined building hubs; routing and siting of plants; interconnections and looped distribution configurations; utility and roadway crossings; resiliency, isolation and valving strategies; evaluation of ties to existing plants or future energy centers; and comparison of electric heat sources such as heat recovery chillers, ambient loop heat pumps, thermal storage, and electric boilers. At building level, the consultant must review records and perform field walkthroughs for identified buildings, classify them into Green/Yellow/Red conversion categories, assess residual steam needs, define domestic hot water strategies, and prepare schematic flow diagrams and control narratives. The assignment also includes load analysis, option comparison, phasing plans, and Class 4/5 opinions of probable cost for campus distribution, building conversions, heat-source equipment, controls integration, and commissioning. The study must address reliability, resiliency, decarbonization, lifecycle value, and constructability while protecting academic, research, and patient-care operations.
services: Professional A/E design and assessment services including feasibility and concept study, campus energy and utility planning, civil engineering input for distribution corridors and crossings, mechanical engineering for heating electrification concepts, rehabilitation/refurbishment planning, programming, architecture/interior coordination, phasing and constructability planning, cost estimating, and preparation of preliminary alignment drawings, schematic flow diagrams, and implementation plans.
relevance_explanation:
- Strategic university campus client and large campus-wide program.
- Early-stage feasibility and concept work can create entry opportunities with broader planning teams.
- Strong sustainability and decarbonization focus aligns with sbp's innovation profile.
- However, the core scope is predominantly mechanical/energy infrastructure planning rather than structural engineering.
- No bridge, long-span roof, special structure, stadium, or complex load-bearing structure is identified.
- Civil engineering input appears limited to utility corridor routing and crossings, not structural design.
- Therefore relevant mainly as a strategic campus/infrastructure study, but only moderately suited to sbp's core expertise.
construction_cost_explanation: No construction budget is stated in the source. The RFP requests only Class 4/5 opinions of probable cost to be developed by the consultant for phased campus distribution, building conversions, heat-source equipment, controls integration, and commissioning. Useful cost drivers mentioned include campus-wide low-temperature hot water distribution, multiple building conversions, new or upgraded heat-source plants, thermal storage, and phased cutovers for academic, research, and patient-care environments.
fee_explanation: No design fee or estimated professional fee is stated in the source.
references_qualifications: Architectural/engineering firms are solicited to provide professional design services. Specific minimum reference or qualification requirements are not stated in the provided source excerpt.

Disciplines requested include Architecture Services, Interior Design/Space Planning, Programming, Rehabilitation & Refurbishment, Civil Engineering, Construction/Project Management, and Mechanical Engineering. Although campus-wide and strategically interesting, the tender is primarily an energy/mechanical feasibility study rather than a structural design commission.
